one_liner: Google's 2D graphics library; its 2016 convolution scaler (Skia 53) resized 4.2x to 9.7x faster than single-threaded ImageMagick 6.8.
what_it_does: Skia is the CPU/GPU 2D drawing engine behind Chrome and Android; image resizing is a side feature reached through SkPixmap::scalePixels / SkImage::scalePixels with SkSamplingOptions, or by drawing an SkImage onto a canvas. The catalogued numbers come from a different, older API: SkBitmapScaler::Resize(dst, src, method) in Skia 53, a standalone separable resampler with box, triangle, Mitchell, Hamming and Lanczos-3 filters. That API was deleted from Skia on 2017-07-20 (commit 'Assume HQ is handled by pipeline, delete legacy code-path'), so it is not a drop-in replacement for ImageMagick's -resize today.
how_it_is_fast: The measured Skia 53 scaler is a two-pass separable convolution over 8-bit BGRA pixels with precomputed per-output-pixel filter taps stored as int16 fixed point (kShiftBits = 14), with SSE2 (x86) and NEON kernels for the horizontal, four-rows-at-once horizontal and vertical passes; that matches the 'Skia 53 SSE2' label in pillow-perf. Current Skia instead resamples by drawing through its raster pipeline: bilinear (2x2 taps) or cubic B/C (fixed 4x4 taps, bicubic_n3x..p3x stages) per output pixel, optional mipmaps for linear filtering, plus a dedicated bicubic_clamp_8888 fast stage.
when_to_use: You already link Skia (Chrome-, Android- or Flutter-style apps, PDF/vector renderers) and need decent-quality thumbnails without adding another imaging library.
Moderate downscales or upscales of 8-bit RGBA/BGRA images where bilinear or Mitchell/Catmull-Rom cubic quality is enough.
Workloads that already draw images to a canvas or GPU surface, where scaling is fused into the draw instead of being a separate pass.
Large-ratio downscales on the CPU using mipmapped linear sampling or SkImage::asyncRescaleAndReadPixels with RescaleMode::kRepeatedLinear / kRepeatedCubic.
when_not_to_use: You want the speed measured here: the SkBitmapScaler code that produced the 4.2x to 9.7x numbers no longer exists in Skia, and no benchmark of current scalePixels against ImageMagick was found.
You need Lanczos or other scale-adaptive convolution filters: current SkSamplingOptions offers only nearest, linear (plus mipmaps) and cubic B/C, and cubic cannot be combined with mipmaps.

You only need a resize kernel: in the same pillow-perf data Pillow-SIMD 4.3 AVX2 needs 0.32x to 0.54x of Skia 53's time (Lanczos 320x200: 6.23 ms vs 18.1 ms on c4.large), so dedicated resizers are faster and much smaller to integrate.
16-bit, float or high-precision resizing pipelines (the measured scaler worked on 8-bit pixels with 14-bit fixed-point weights).
Projects that cannot take a GN/Ninja build with Python-driven dependency sync, Clang and C++20.

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (GN + Ninja; is_component_build for shared)
integration.dependencies: Python 3 for tools/git-sync-deps and bin/fetch-gn; GN and Ninja; third-party codecs and fonts (libpng, libjpeg-turbo, libwebp, FreeType, ICU, etc.) are optional per skia_use_* flags; Bazel for some Rust third-party code; CMake 3.30+ only for Dawn
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (site/docs/user/build.md); Clang strongly preferred, since software-rasterizer and color-conversion paths are documented to be 'dramatically' slower with GCC or MSVC
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS, ChromeOS; x86-64 and arm64 CPU paths, plus GPU backends
integration.thread_safety: SkBitmap is not thread-safe (each thread needs its own SkBitmap, pixel memory may be shared); SkPixelRef is thread-safe; one surface/canvas per thread
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — a library call (SkPixmap::scalePixels) rather than ImageMagick's CLI/MagickWand API, with no codec-to-codec pipeline, no Lanczos and no 16-bit quantum depth

gotchas: The measured API (SkBitmapScaler, SkConvolver, SkResizeFilter) was removed on 2017-07-20; nanobench numbers for Skia 53 do not describe any Skia release after that.

Current cubic sampling uses a fixed 4x4 footprint per output pixel, so very large downscales with cubic alias unless you downscale in steps (asyncRescaleAndReadPixels kRepeatedCubic) or use mipmapped linear sampling.
Skia has no stable API: RELEASE_NOTES.md lists removals and signature changes almost every milestone, so pin a milestone branch (chrome/mNNN).
Chromium still carries the old convolution resizer (skia::ImageOperations::Resize in skia/ext, Lanczos-3/box/Hamming with SSE2, NEON and LSX), but it lives in the Chromium tree, not in Skia.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Skia when it is already in the binary and you also need drawing or GPU compositing; for a standalone fast resizer, Pillow-SIMD's resample code (faster than Skia 53 in the same dataset), libvips or OpenCV are better choices, and stb-image-resize-opt is the lightweight single-header option.
verified_claims_summary: pillow-perf (python-pillow) timed Skia 53's SSE2 SkBitmapScaler in a C++ nanobench loop on a white 2560x1600 N32 bitmap against ImageMagick 6.8.9-9 through Python Wand with MAGICK_THREAD_LIMIT=1 on an RGB image, on a Xeon E5-2666 v3 (c4.large, Ubuntu 16.04.1) and a Core i5-4258U; Skia was 6.4x to 9.5x and 4.2x to 9.7x faster across 12 size/filter cases (derived from page data), with no compiler or flags recorded. The harnesses are not symmetric: the Skia loop reuses a destination preallocated outside the timed loop, while each ImageMagick run includes a clone, a fresh result image and Python call overhead.
status_note: Very actively developed (last commit 2026-10-03; RELEASE_NOTES.md already has a Milestone 156 section) and BSD-3-Clause, so copyable, but the benchmarked scaler was deleted in 2017 and today's equivalent is an unbenchmarked raster-pipeline path.
